title: GPU supply tactical plan: phased onboarding and runway by region (NA/EU/APAC)
summary: Tactical supply plan that sequences GPU onboarding across NA, EU, and APAC for 2026 with explicit procurement cadence, staging pools, utilization targets, and risk mitigations. Focused on reducing single-region risk and preserving latency SLO headroom while minimizing committed spend.
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a pragmatic, phased approach to adding GPU capacity across cloud regions (North America, Europe, APAC) for 2026. It reconciles expected demand growth, procurement lead times, and model/instance compatibility constraints. It emphasizes three objectives: preserve latency headroom for hosted customers, avoid overcommitment on model-specific SKUs, and create regional staging pools for safe rollouts to Dedicated and Private customers.

High-level principles and assumptions:
- Growth: baseline token-serving QPS growth of 35% net-quarter from current Feb 2026 levels; spikes up to +80% modeled for PLG campaign bursts.
- Utilization target band: 45–65% steady-state for hosted pools to maintain latency SLOs and absorb variance.
- Preferred GPU mix: H100 (mixed-precision serving for large model families) + L4 (cost-effective for smaller models/embeddings). A100 inventory considered only for existing on-prem compatibility.
- Procurement lead times: committed reserved instances (cloud marketplace) 6–10 weeks to appear; custom hardware/procurement for private deployments 12–20 weeks.
- Cost sensitivity: finance will cap incremental committed spend to $X/month growth per region (see linked artifact INFRA-842 for raw numbers).
- Compatibility: quantized model variants reduce per-token cost by ~22% — included as offset to effective capacity.

Regional staging strategy (phased onboarding):
- Phase 0 (warm-up, immediate): shift 10% of cross-region burst capacity into NA warm pool using spot/ephemeral L4s—target deploy by 2026-03-15. Purpose: short-term latency headroom for NA.
- Phase 1 (Q2 2026): Provision initial H100-backed pool in NA (x64 GPUs) to serve medium-to-large models; enable prefix caching and continuous batching. Concurrent EU pool (x24 GPUs) with mixed H100/L4 to test routing fallbacks.
- Phase 2 (Q3 2026): Expand APAC warm pool (x32 L4) to reduce inter-region egress for APAC customers. Convert 50% of NA spot capacity into reserved H100 capacity if utilization >55% for 4 consecutive weeks.
- Phase 3 (Q4 2026): Finalize Dedicated-ready pools per region (NA: x192, EU: x96, APAC: x64 target allocations) aligned to committed customer demand profiles and SLAs.

Quarterly capacity matrix (target GPUs by region; numbers are physical GPU units):
Region | Q2 2026 target | Q3 2026 target | Q4 2026 target
NA     | 64 (H100=48, L4=16) | 128 (H100=96, L4=32) | 192 (H100=144, L4=48)
EU     | 24 (H100=12, L4=12) | 48 (H100=36, L4=12) | 96 (H100=72, L4=24)
APAC   | 16 (L4=16)          | 32 (L4=32)           | 64 (L4=48, H100=16)

Utilization and burn model (simplified):
- Effective serving capacity = raw GPUs * model-efficiency factor (empirically ~0.75 for H100 mixed workloads; 0.6 for L4 when used for larger models).
- Expected steady-state utilization s.t. headroom >= 35% for tail latency recovery on 99p.
- If observed utilization > 70% for 2 weeks, trigger immediate temporary burst requests to partner regions and open procurement pipeline for reserved capacity.

Operational runbooks and rollout constraints:
- Canary window: enable new pool at 10% traffic for 72 hours with linear increase only if key latency percentiles (p95/p99) do not degrade >15% relative to baseline.
- Model compatibility check: ensure CUDA and Triton stack parity across regions before routing traffic. Run compatibility matrix from linked Confluence doc (driver/torch/cu versions).
- KV cache priming: use historical request prefixes to pre-populate KV cache on new nodes to minimize cold-start tail latency during rollouts.

Risk register and mitigations:
- Risk: Cloud SKU discontinuation or price shock. Mitigation: maintain convertible capacity profile (L4-heavy warm pools), commit only to short-duration reserved terms in volatile markets.
- Risk: Procurement delays for private deployments. Mitigation: maintain a 12-week buffer of skewed spot capacity and document migration plan to on-prem.
- Risk: Regional network outages causing capacity shortfall. Mitigation: cross-region routing policy with automated fallback to secondary region and automatic customer-facing degraded mode.

Key action items (owner — ETA):
- Finalize H100 vs L4 allocation decision for Q2 purchases — Marco Liu (procurement) — 2026-03-10.
- Implement warm-pool autoscaling policy (spot->reserved conversion triggers) — Luis Ortega — 2026-04-01.
- Publish updated canary rollout checklist and add to console automation — Jenna Morales (SRE) + DevEx — 2026-03-25.
- Finance alignment on incremental commit cap and runway numbers — Priya Shah — 2026-03-05.
- Create runbook for cross-region emergency re-routing (test playbook) — Elliot Barnes — 2026-04-12.

Monitoring and KPIs to watch pre/post onboarding:
- Region token throughput (tokens/min) and token latency p95/p99 by model family.
- GPU-level utilization distribution (per-instance percentile) and 1h rolling average.
- Reserved vs spot ratio and monthly committed spend delta.
- Canary degradation rate (percent of canaries failing threshold checks).

Notes and open questions (for leadership meeting):
- Decide if we accelerate APAC H100 buys given partner demand in Singapore (lead time tradeoff vs temporary L4 warm pool).
- Confirm acceptable utilization ceiling for Dedicated customer SLAs before we convert spot capacity into reserved commitments.
- Validate that Private on-prem sizing templates align with the Q4 Dedicated pool targets (avoid double-counting).

Appendix: quick reference decision rules (short):
- Rule A: If NA 1h utilization > 60% for 10 business days, increase NA reserved buys by 32 GPUs next procurement cycle.
- Rule B: If EU latency p99 increases >20% post-rollout, automatically reduce traffic to EU pool by 30% and convert traffic to NA fallback for 72 hours.
- Rule C: If overall platform growth quarter-over-quarter < 20%, defer non-essential reserved purchases by one cycle.

This document is a working tactical sheet intended to be iterated after the next capacity review on 2026-03-15. Feedback welcome — tag owners in comments and link any missing demand signals (sales/CS commitments) under linked_artifacts.
